title: Telemundo, U.S. Soccer agree Spanish-language rights deal for USMNT, USWNT matches until 2030
content:
Telemundo will remain the exclusive Spanish-language broadcasting network for the United States’ men’s and women’s national teams until 2030 following a new agreement with U.S. Soccer.

In a press release issued on Wednesday, the network said it will continue to broadcast “more than 20 U.S. National Team matches annually” across Telemundo, Universo, Peacock and Telemundo’s digital platforms.

The coverage, which extends across the U.S. and its territories, features the men’s and women’s national teams, encompassing “high-profile international friendlies, the SheBelieves Cup and select competitions such as the CONCACAF Nations League”.

U.S. Soccer Youth National Team matches will also be featured under the renewed agreement, which Telemundo says will help in “expanding visibility across U.S. Soccer’s full pathway”.

David Wright. U.S. Soccer’s chief commercial officer, said: “We’re excited to build on our partnership with Telemundo in bringing U.S. Soccer to Spanish-speaking fans throughout the country.

“Telemundo plays a critical role in how we connect with one of the most passionate and influential fan bases in the country. As we look ahead to 2026 and beyond, this partnership is about more than distribution. It’s about reaching new audiences, deepening engagement, and ensuring more fans can see and follow our teams in the moments that matter most.”

The renewed deal builds upon Telemundo’s expanding portfolio, with the network broadcasting 92 of the 104 matches taking place at this summer’s World Cup, making up 700 hours of World Cup programming throughout the 39-day tournament. Executive vice-president of sports Joaquin Duro claimed to The Athletic the network’s World Cup coverage plan is “most ambitious” in its history.

Telemundo agreed an initial four-year deal in 2023 to show more than 20 matches across the USMNT and USWNT, following U.S. Soccer’s split from Soccer United Marketing. The network also held Spanish-language rights to the 2022 men’s World Cup, 2023 women’s World Cup and 2024 Olympic Games.

“We’re proud to extend our partnership with U.S. Soccer and continue serving as the Spanish-language home for the Men’s and Women’s National Teams,” said Duro. “From friendlies to major tournaments, this agreement gives us the opportunity to follow the teams’ journey and engage audiences across every platform in the years leading up to 2030.”
